name: gauche
desc: R7RS Scheme implementation, developed to be a handy script interpreter
why: A capable R7RS Scheme with a long history, a classic Lisp worth exploring beyond the usual interpreters.

brief.what_it_is: Gauche is an R7RS Scheme implementation aimed at scripting and real-world programming. It runs Scheme programs from the command line (the homepage shows a script that builds an SVG file and writes it to disk). The page says it ships with networking, Unicode strings, regular expressions, threads, and common algorithms and data structures built in. It also has lazy sequences, an object system with a metaobject protocol, and a package manager with over 200 libraries and extensions.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents Gauche as a Scheme for practical scripting, with quick startup time and smooth integration with the operating system, suitable for automation, build tools, and shell-like scripting.
brief.install_notes: The homepage has a 'Download Gauche' button with latest release 0.9.15 and a 'Documentation' link, but gives no install steps, dependencies, or first-run instructions. Packages are managed with the gauche-package command, which the homepage mentions in text only. The installed executables listed in the metadata are gauche-cesconv, gauche-config, gauche-install, gauche-package, and gosh.
brief.standout: Gauche combines a small, fast-starting Scheme for scripting with batteries included and a lot of language extension: integrated lazy sequences (the homepage example uses generator->lseq and lmap-accum to build an infinite Fibonacci list), and a CLOS-like object system with a metaobject protocol. The homepage example is a short Scheme program that produces an SVG spiral file.
brief.status: Maintained, by the evidence on the homepage: latest release 0.9.15 and a news item dated 2025/12/14 announcing a Gauche-gtk2 0.6.2 update. The page says it has been developed and used for over two decades. I did not see a dated commit history or the release date for 0.9.15.
brief.caveats: The homepage makes no claims about supported platforms, licensing, or build requirements, and I did not open the documentation, so those are unverified. The Documentation and extension-browser links did not give URLs in the fetched text, so I did not follow them. The homepage is a marketing-style page, so performance claims ('fast') are the project's own wording.
quotes: A fast, practical R7RS Scheme implementation for scripting and real-world programming.
Gauche emphasizes quick startup time, smooth integration with the operating system, and expressive syntax, making it suitable for automation, build tools, and shell-like scripting.
Developed and used for over two decades, Gauche focuses on stability, backward compatibility, and long-term maintainability.
fetch_log: https://practical-scheme.net/gauche/ - loaded (homepage, text extracted; contains the release, feature summary, and Fibonacci example). Documentation and extension-browser pages were not fetched because their URLs were not present in the text.
